title: Hamlet's Mill on ancient knowledge of precession

tellings.quote: very ancient very early knowledge of of precession.

plain: Graham Hancock, a writer about lost ancient civilisations, points to Hamlet's Mill, a 1960s book by Giorgio de Santillana of MIT, a US university, and Hertha von Dechend of Frankfurt University. Hancock says the book argues that ancient myths carry very early knowledge of precession, the slow wobble of the Earth that shifts the stars' positions over thousands of years. If true, people in the distant past knew far more astronomy than is usually thought.
